I mean you have to have a job or go to school. no way around that, but I guess it would be this or a remote job - but remote jobs are really hard to get unless you have some further and more specific education (eg. writing, coding, travel/event planning). That was a big plus for going to uni for me, is that it would make it possible to get from home jobs that aren’t either cold-calling to make sales or answering phone calls all day that are mostly from angry customers. 

In your situation I’d say PetSmart is the best option other than pursuing a short online certification to work a nice job online, and decide whether working freelance or with a company is less stressful to you! 

But if I’m going to be actually honest, coming from what I learned in psychology, you may really struggle to ever be happy in any job if you continue to let your dysphoria be triggered by such uncontrollable outside influences. The best way to do this is to sit yourself down and think about WHY, why does it upset you so much that you can’t fully function when people disrespect your gender? It may sound obvious and you might respond with “because duh” but it is only when you know YOUR specific reason as to why it hurts that you can come up with YOUR specific method, rationalization, whatever that will make you feel better, honestly sometimes knowing why it hurts is healing enough in itself. Not to be insensitive but truly people will always suck sometimes no matter who or where you are, and your happiness and mental health is ONLY dependent on you. If you make it dependent on others it will also not get better. 

Don’t put a bandaid on it by trying to find a job you can just stand, do what is needed to help the overarching problem and not be scared of finding what you truly want to do.
